requirements.text: Assets can be transferred within the same department without a request.
Inter-departmental asset transfers must be approved by a DA group member and a faculty group member.
Inter-faculty asset transfers must be approved by a faculty group or higher level.
Asset transfers outside the university must be approved by the university group.
Administrative level users or inventory users can edit assets belonging to their department, faculty, or university if authorized.
All fields of an edited asset can be modified except IDs.
A bulk entry file can be used for modifying assets.
Any DA group member or authorized inventory group member can add assets owned by the department.
Any faculty member can add all related departments' inventory.
Any university group member can add all assets in the inventory.
A bulk entry can be used to add many assets.
Requests can be made by any authorized user.
An inventory user must check returned assets and update the inventory.
IT group members can create a new space and modify floor structure upon receiving an exception request.
Authorized administrative or inventory group members can display and approve pending requests.
Users are notified by email when a request is treated.
Requests are added to the waiting for execution list after approval.
Inventory is updated when a user receives the requested asset.
Authentication is performed via username and password for all users.
Administrative level users can delegate authorized actions to other users.

The system shall enforce a password policy requiring a minimum of 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters, and implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts.
All data transmissions between the client and server must be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher, and sensitive data at rest must be encrypted using AES-256.

The system shall maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, asset modifications, and permission changes, including user ID, timestamp, and action details, retained for a minimum of 1 year.
Access to database servers shall be restricted to authorized IT personnel via multi-factor authentication, and all administrative database access must be logged and reviewed periodically.
The system shall maintain 99.9% availability during university working hours (08:00-18:00, Mon-Fri).
The system shall terminate any database query that exceeds 60 seconds of execution time to prevent resource exhaustion under peak load.
The system shall perform daily incremental backups with an RPO of 24 hours and an RTO of 4 hours.
The system shall follow a modular architecture (e.g., MVC or Microservices) to ensure that changes to the inventory logic do not require modifications to the authentication or reporting modules.
The system shall support a minimum of [X] concurrent users and [Y] transactions per minute during peak working hours without exceeding a 2-second response time.
The system shall process bulk entry files of up to [X] records within [Y] seconds.
Standard search queries shall return results within [X] milliseconds for a dataset of [Y] records.
The system shall be designed to scale to [X] million assets while maintaining sub-second search latency.
